items.answer: C = 761 + 12n, R = 27n; break-even n = 51; e.g. costs per shirt may fall with bulk buying

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "parabola"?
options: A function y = ax² + bx + c used when the rate of change itself changes steadily, e.g. projectile height
The vertical line through the vertex about which the parabola is symmetric, x = −b/(2a)
A function of the form y = mx + c used when a quantity changes at a constant rate
The U-shaped graph of a quadratic function
items.answer: The U-shaped graph of a quadratic function
items.markingKey: D. "parabola" is the U-shaped graph of a quadratic function.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "A relation in which every input in the domain has exactly one output"?
items.answer: function
items.markingKey: A. This is the definition of function.

items.stem: State what is meant by the term "composite function".
items.answer: F(g(x)), the result of applying g first and then f
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: f(g(x)), the result of applying g first and then f. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: A linear model predicts a plant’s height h = 0.5t + 1 cm after t days. Explain why it should not be used for t = 1000.
items.answer: Plants stop growing at a constant rate; extrapolating so far outside the observed data is unreliable.
items.markingKey: Plants stop growing at a constant rate; extrapolating so far outside the observed data is unreliable. (R1 R1)

items.stem: A parabola has x-intercepts at 1 and 2. Explain how you can find its axis of symmetry without knowing its equation.
items.markingKey: The axis is midway between the roots by symmetry (R1): x = (1 + 2)/2 = 3/2 (A1).

items.stem: Explain why f(x) = 1/(x − 2) has a restricted domain and state it.
items.answer: Division by zero is undefined at x = 2; domain x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 2.
items.markingKey: Division by zero is undefined at x = 2; domain x ∈ ℝ, x ≠ 2. (R1 A1)

items.stem: "If f(x) = 3x + 1, then f(x + 2) = 3x + 3." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Replace x by (x + 2): 3(x + 2) + 1 = 3x + 7.
items.markingKey: Replace x by (x + 2): 3(x + 2) + 1 = 3x + 7. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: A linear model predicts a plant’s height h = 0.9t + 3 cm after t days. Explain why it should not be used for t = 1000.
items.answer: Plants stop growing at a constant rate; extrapolating so far outside the observed data is unreliable.
items.markingKey: Plants stop growing at a constant rate; extrapolating so far outside the observed data is unreliable. (R1 R1)

items.stem: "The vertex of y = (x + 4)² − 1 is (4, −1)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: x + 4 = 0 when x = −4, so the vertex is (−4, −1).
items.markingKey: x + 4 = 0 when x = −4, so the vertex is (−4, −1). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Does the set of ordered pairs {(3, 8), (-2, 0), (2, -2), (5, 4)} represent a function? Give a reason.
items.answer: Yes
items.markingKey: Yes: every first coordinate appears once (R1). A1 for the decision.

items.stem: f(x) = 4x + 8. Find the value of x for which f(x) = −12.
The table shows x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and y = 28, 30, 36, 46, 60. Decide whether a linear or quadratic model fits, find the model, and use it to predict y when x = 6.
items.answer: quadratic: y = 2x² + 28; y(6) = 100
items.markingKey: Constant second differences of 4 (R1); model (M1 A1); prediction (A1).

items.stem: For y = 2x² − 2x − 4, find the x-intercepts, the y-intercept, the axis of symmetry and the vertex.
items.markingKey: Factorise or formula for roots (A1); y-intercept −4 (A1); axis x = 1/2 (A1); vertex (1/2, −9/2) (A1).

items.stem: State the domain and range of f(x) = x² + 6.
items.answer: domain all real x; range f(x) ≥ 6
items.markingKey: domain all real x; range f(x) ≥ 6 (A1 domain, A1 range; correct notation C1).

items.stem: Given f(x) = 3x² − 6x + 9, find f(−4) and f(−5).
items.markingKey: Correct substitution with brackets for negatives (M1); f(−4) = 81, f(−5) = 114 (A1 A1).

items.stem: The table shows x = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and y = 26, 33, 40, 47, 54. Decide whether a linear or quadratic model fits, find the model, and use it to predict y when x = 6.
items.answer: linear: y = 7x + 26; y(6) = 68
items.markingKey: Constant first differences of 7 (R1); model (M1 A1); prediction (A1).

items.stem: A parabola crosses the x-axis at x = 5 and x = 3 and passes through (4, −2). Find its equation in the form y = ax² + bx + c.
items.markingKey: Use intercept form y = a(x − r₁)(x − r₂) (M1); substitute the extra point to find a (M1 A1); final equation y = 2x² − 16x + 30 (A1).

items.stem: Leila rents bikes: the cost C(h) = 4h euros for h whole hours, up to 8 hours. List the domain and range, and explain whether a graph of C should be drawn as a continuous line.
items.answer: domain {1, …, 8}, range {4, 8, …, 32}; discrete points only
